newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to go ahead with Weld nomination.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to go ahead with Weld nomination.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will formally nominate Massachusetts Gov. William Weld to be U.S. ambassador to Mexico "very shortly" despite powerful Senate opposition, the White House said on Monday.

Weld, a moderate Republican, is bitterly opposed by Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms, a conservative North Carolina Republican who objects to his support for medical use of marijuana, among other things.
Helms' objections notwithstanding, "I anticipate quite shortly that we will formally send the nomination to the Senate," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
McCurry said winning confirmation for Weld "will require clearly an extensive effort on our part to try to press the case for the nomination."
"It will be difficult, but we hope not impossible," McCurry said.

Weld charged last week that Helms' opposition was political. "This is about ideological purity. And whether there is only one kind of Republican welcomed in the Republican Party ... That's what this is about," he said.
